thread:
AcmeApp: Hey team — our production calls all started failing with 429s at ~2026-03-31 16:12 PDT. We drained our monthly credits earlier than expected, customer says they did a big run at midday. Can someone confirm when monthly credits actually refill?

Maya Nguyen: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the response headers from one of the 429s and the org id? Also which timezone is your billing account set to?

AcmeApp: header snippet: `x-rw-remaining-tokens: 0`, `x-rw-reset-ts: 1712016000` (not sure what that ts is), org_id: org_01G7X2

Jorge Ruiz: Thanks — that reset ts looks weird. I'll query the credit endpoint. Give me 2 min.

quota-bot: automated-check: org org_01G7X2 current_credits=0 next_refill=2026-04-01T00:00:00-07:00 billing_timezone=America/Los_Angeles burst_window=30s burst_pool=5e5

Alicia Chen: Quick note on billing: our refill logic runs at 00:00 in the org's billing timezone, not UTC. UI sometimes displays the refill as "end of day" without timezone which confuses folks.

Maya Nguyen: @AcmeApp — looks like your org is set to America/Los_Angeles, so a refill at 00:00 PDT. That means if you consumed credits on Mar 31 at 16:12 PDT you'll only get refill at 00:00 on Apr 1 PDT. That's ~8 hours later, which can feel like "early" exhaustion if you expected a UTC midnight reset.

AcmeApp: Huh — we assumed it was a rolling 30-day window, not monthly anchored to a timezone. Can Redwood do rolling instead?

Jorge Ruiz: Right now hosted plans use a billing-cycle anchor (monthly) not rolling window. Rolling token buckets are an internal feature request but not how monthly credits are currently calculated.

Maya Nguyen: For immediate relief I can provision a temporary top-up so your jobs can finish. Do you want a one-off 200k token emergency grant?

AcmeApp: Yes please, that would help. Also can we change our billing timezone to UTC so future refills align with our infra timing?

Alicia Chen: You can change billing timezone in Console > Org Settings > Billing timezone. Note: changing the timezone will move the anchor for future refills — it does NOT retroactively move past refill timestamps. If you change it now your next refill will occur at 00:00 in the new tz on the next cycle boundary.

Maya Nguyen: Granting 200k now. ETA ~30s.

deploy-bot: action: grant_credits org=org_01G7X2 amount=200000 reason="support emergency" by=MayaNguyen job_id=jb_2026_304_77 status=done

AcmeApp: Confirmed — calls resumed, thank you!

Jorge Ruiz: Follow-ups for us: 1) small doc update to Console billing page to show timezone explicitly and explain anchor behavior, 2) product ticket to evaluate rolling-window vs anchored monthly for consumption plans, 3) ops check if `x-rw-reset-ts` header is returning epoch in local tz vs UTC (that timestamp looked off). I'm filing those now.

Maya Nguyen: Repro steps for internal ticket: 1) set org tz to a non-UTC zone (e.g., America/Los_Angeles), 2) consume all credits before local midnight, 3) observe refill at local 00:00 next day, 4) confirm Console UI label shows tz (or not) and header `x-rw-reset-ts` corresponds to next_refill in org timezone. Paste logs to the ticket.

Alicia Chen: Billing note: for customers who need continuous availability we recommend Dedicated or Reserved capacity — those aren't governed by monthly token refills. Also we can offer scheduled top-ups for heavy end-of-month runs.

AcmeApp: Appreciate the quick help. Please keep me posted on the doc + product tickets, we want to avoid surprises next month.

Maya Nguyen: Will do — follow-up tickets: DOC-456 (Console tz copy), PROD-789 (rolling-window eval), INFRA-112 (header epoch sanity). I'll CC billing and product. Closing this thread when tickets are linked. :thumbsup:
